text:
Marathon Petroleum rose 0.24% today, capping a volatile two-week rally of 13.2% that reflects surging oil prices and geopolitical tension. Brent crude touched $110 this week as Iran escalated attacks in the Strait of Hormuz, and U.S. crude broke past $101—a sharp move upward. U.S. refineries are running at 93.5% capacity with healthy inventory levels, positioning refiners like Marathon to benefit from wider profit margins when crude spikes while product demand remains steady.

The broader story here is that oil prices are being pushed higher by shipping disruptions (tanker rates have surged, effectively adding $30–$40 to the real cost of delivering physical oil) and Middle East conflict, while Trump's stated reluctance to escalate militarily into Iran has relieved some tail-risk selling pressure. Refiner stocks like Marathon typically gain when crude rises sharply because they buy cheap feedstock and sell refined products at prices that don't always fall as fast—that margin expansion has driven the recent run-up.
